answer: Each voyage enters the atlas by surveying one new ledge. Each identity locks a 70-credit bond, fixes the ledge by two bearings, and files it in the atlas. Any peer recomputes the ledge from the bearings; a miss over 50 metres burns the bond. First survey 32 credits, the k-th 32+7(k-1): 1,000 fakes cost 3,528,500. A phantom-ledge ring fails: a voyage with an invented ledge cannot triangulate. An honest surveyor pays 32 once, bond reclaimed.
